title: 국내 여행
intro: 국내 여행은 '좋아하는 여행지 묘사 → 여행 준비 루틴 → 기억에 남는 여행 경험 → 과거와 현재 비교' 순서로 자주 출제됩니다. 친구 Minji와 함께 간 부산(해운대, 돼지국밥)과 가족과 함께 간 제주 두 가지 이야기만 준비해 두면 거의 모든 질문에 재활용할 수 있습니다. 바쁜 대학생 일상에서 벗어나 쉬는 시간이라는 감정 포인트를 꼭 넣으세요.
strategy: 답변 흐름: 시작 문장(Sure, I'd love to talk about ~) → 어디/누구와/어떻게 가는지 기본 정보 → 거기서 하는 일·먹은 음식 세부 → 좋아하는 이유·느낌 → 마무리 문장(So yeah, that's why I really like ~)
여행지는 부산(친구들과, 바다·해운대·돼지국밥)과 제주(가족과)로 고정해서 묘사·경험·비교 질문에 같은 장면을 돌려 쓰세요.
KTX로 2시간 반, 해운대 해변, 바다가 보이는 카페처럼 구체적인 숫자와 장소 이름을 하나씩 넣으면 IH 이상으로 들립니다.
비교 질문은 '고등학생 때는 부모님이 다 계획 → 지금은 친구들과 앱으로 직접 계획'처럼 과거/현재 시제를 분명히 나눠 말하세요.

expressions.en: Sure, I'd love to talk about my favorite place in Korea.
expressions.ko: 네, 제가 한국에서 제일 좋아하는 곳에 대해 말해 볼게요.
expressions.note: 국내 여행 질문의 시작 문장으로 그대로 사용

expressions.en: It takes about two and a half hours by KTX.
expressions.ko: KTX로 두 시간 반 정도 걸려요.

expressions.en: I usually go there with my friends.
The food was really cheap and delicious.
I took a lot of pictures.
I pack light, just a small backpack.
expressions.ko: 저는 짐을 가볍게 싸요, 작은 배낭 하나만요.

expressions.en: It was a nice break from my busy school life.
It's pretty easy to get there.
We booked everything on our phones.
Being near the ocean really helps me clear my head.
expressions.ko: 바다 근처에 있으면 머리가 정말 맑아져요.

expressions.en: Back in high school, my parents planned everything.
expressions.ko: 고등학교 때는 부모님이 모든 걸 계획하셨어요.
expressions.note: 과거 비교의 시작 표현 Back in ~

expressions.en: So yeah, that's why I really like Busan.
expressions.ko: 그래서 제가 부산을 정말 좋아하는 거예요.
expressions.note: 마무리 문장. 장소 이름만 바꿔서 사용

expressions.en: It was one of those trips I'll never forget.
expressions.ko: 절대 잊지 못할 그런 여행 중 하나였어요.

expressions.en: Honestly, it's the kind of place that makes you want to come back.
expressions.ko: 솔직히 다시 오고 싶게 만드는 그런 곳이에요.
expressions.note: the kind of place that ~ : ~하는 그런 곳

questions.en: You indicated in the survey that you enjoy traveling within your country. Tell me about a place in Korea that you like to visit. Where is it, what is it like, and why do you like it?
questions.ko: 설문에서 국내 여행을 즐긴다고 하셨습니다. 한국에서 즐겨 가는 곳에 대해 말해 주세요. 어디에 있고, 어떤 곳이며, 왜 좋아하나요?
tips: 답변 흐름: 시작 문장 → 장소 이름·위치·가는 방법 → 거기서 하는 일(해변 산책, 음식) → 좋아하는 이유 → 'So yeah, that's why ~' 마무리
부산 = 친구들, 해운대, 돼지국밥으로 고정하면 경험 질문에서도 그대로 쓸 수 있어요.
'바쁜 서울 생활에서 벗어나 쉰다'는 이유를 넣으면 자연스럽게 감정이 들어갑니다.

answers.IM3: Okay, let me tell you about my favorite place in Korea. It's Busan. Busan is a big city by the sea, and it takes about two and a half hours from Seoul by KTX. I usually go there with my friends from school. My favorite spot is Haeundae Beach. We walk along the beach and take a lot of pictures. We also eat dwaeji-gukbap. It's a hot pork soup, and it's really cheap and delicious. I like Busan because I can relax by the ocean. Yeah, that's my favorite place in Korea.
answers.IH: Sure, I'd love to talk about my favorite place in Korea. It's definitely Busan. Busan is the second biggest city in Korea, and it's right next to the sea. It only takes about two and a half hours from Seoul by KTX, so it's pretty easy to get there. I've been there a few times with my close friend Minji and some other friends from my major. The best part is Haeundae Beach. The sand is soft, the water is really blue, and at night the city lights look so pretty. We usually walk along the beach, grab some coffee at a café with an ocean view, and just talk for hours. And of course, we always eat dwaeji-gukbap. It's a hot pork soup with rice, and honestly, it tastes way better in Busan than in Seoul. My life in Seoul is pretty busy, so being near the ocean really helps me clear my head. So yeah, that's why I really like Busan.
answers.AL: Oh, a place in Korea I like to visit? Let me think. I'd have to say Busan. It's the second biggest city in Korea, and what I love about it is that it has both a big city vibe and the ocean. It only takes about two and a half hours from Seoul by KTX, so it's perfect for a short weekend trip. I usually go with my best friend Minji and a couple of other friends from my business classes. The first place we always go is Haeundae Beach. During the day, we walk along the beach barefoot, and in the evening we sit on the sand and watch the city lights come on. It's honestly so peaceful. Then there's the food. Busan is famous for dwaeji-gukbap, which is a hot pork soup with rice. It's cheap, it's filling, and it's the kind of comfort food you crave after a long day of walking around. My weekdays in Seoul are pretty hectic because I have so many classes, so when I'm in Busan, I feel like I can finally breathe. Honestly, it's the kind of place that makes you want to come back again and again. So yeah, that's pretty much why Busan is my favorite place in Korea.

questions.en: How do you usually plan and prepare for a trip within Korea? Who do you usually travel with, what do you pack, and what do you do before you leave?
questions.ko: 국내 여행을 보통 어떻게 계획하고 준비하나요? 주로 누구와 여행하고, 무엇을 챙기며, 떠나기 전에 무엇을 하나요?
tips: 답변 흐름: 시작 문장 → 누구와 가는지 → 준비 순서(날짜 정하기 → KTX·숙소 예약 → 맛집 찾기 → 짐 싸기) → 준비하면서 드는 느낌 → 마무리
First, Then, After that, Finally 같은 순서 연결어를 쓰면 루틴이 깔끔하게 들립니다.
현재 시제(습관)로 일관되게 말하고, 'usually', 'always' 같은 빈도 부사를 넣으세요.

answers.IM3: Sure, let me tell you how I plan a trip in Korea. I usually travel with my friends, especially my friend Minji. First, we pick a date. It's usually on the weekend or during vacation. Then we book KTX tickets and a small hotel on our phones. After that, we look for good restaurants online. I pack light, just a small backpack with some clothes, a charger, and sunscreen. Planning is pretty fun for me. Yeah, that's how I usually get ready for a trip.
answers.IH: Okay, let me tell you about how I prepare for a trip in Korea. I usually travel with my friends from school, especially my close friend Minji. Since we're both business majors, we're pretty busy during the semester, so first we check our class schedules and pick a weekend or a vacation week. Then we book KTX tickets right away, because they sell out really fast on weekends. After that, we find a cheap but clean place to stay on a booking app. The fun part is searching for restaurants. We look at reviews and make a list of places we want to try, like a famous gukbap place in Busan. The night before, I pack light, just a small backpack with a few clothes, a phone charger, sunscreen, and my earphones for the train. Honestly, the planning is almost as exciting as the trip itself. So yeah, that's pretty much how I get ready for a trip.
answers.AL: Oh, how I prepare for a trip in Korea? Let me think. Well, I usually travel with my friends, and my best friend Minji is pretty much always with me. The first step is the hardest one, which is finding a time that works for everyone. We're all college students with tons of classes and part-time jobs, so we compare our schedules in our group chat and usually end up picking a long weekend. Once the date is set, we book KTX tickets right away, because if you wait even a few days, all the good seats are gone. Then we look for a place to stay. We don't need anything fancy, just somewhere clean and close to the subway. After that comes my favorite part, which is making a food list. Minji is in charge of cafés, and I'm in charge of restaurants, so we kind of turn it into a little competition. The night before we leave, I pack light, because I hate carrying a heavy bag around. I just bring a small backpack with a couple of outfits, a charger, sunscreen, and my earphones so I can listen to IU on the train. Yeah, that's basically how I get ready for a trip with my friends.

questions.en: Tell me about a memorable trip you took in Korea. When was it, where did you go, who were you with, and what happened that made it so memorable?
questions.ko: 한국에서 다녀온 기억에 남는 여행에 대해 말해 주세요. 언제, 어디로, 누구와 갔고, 어떤 일이 있어서 기억에 남나요?
tips: 답변 흐름: 시작 문장 → 언제·어디·누구와 → 일어난 일 순서대로(과거 시제) → 그때의 감정 → 'That's why it was so memorable' 마무리
가족과 간 제주 여행을 쓰면 부산(친구) 이야기와 겹치지 않아 다양하게 들립니다.
비가 왔다, 길을 잃었다 같은 작은 사건(문제 → 해결)을 하나 넣으면 IH 이상으로 올라갑니다.

answers.IM3: Oh, a memorable trip? Let me think. It was a trip to Jeju Island with my family. My mom, my dad, my brother Junho, and I went there a few years ago. We rented a car and drove around the island. We saw the beautiful ocean and climbed a small mountain. On the second day, it rained a lot, so we went to a museum and ate black pork. It was really good. We laughed a lot together. Yeah, that's my most memorable trip in Korea.
answers.IH: Sure, I'd love to talk about a memorable trip. It was a family trip to Jeju Island a few years ago. My mom, my dad, my younger brother Junho, and I flew there for four days. It was our first big family trip in a long time, so everyone was really excited. We rented a car, and my dad drove us all around the island. We saw the ocean, walked along a coastal trail, and climbed a small volcano called Seongsan Ilchulbong. But on the third day, it suddenly started pouring rain, and all our plans were ruined. At first, Junho and I were really disappointed. But then my mom found a cozy restaurant, and we ate black pork barbecue while we listened to the rain. We talked and laughed for hours. That night actually became the best part of the trip. That's why it was so memorable for me.
answers.AL: Oh, a memorable trip in Korea? Let me think. Definitely the family trip I took to Jeju Island a few years ago. It was me, my mom, my dad, and my younger brother Junho, and it was our first real family trip in years, because everyone was always so busy. We flew to Jeju, rented a car, and my dad, who's honestly a pretty nervous driver, drove us all over the island. On the first two days, everything went perfectly. We hiked up Seongsan Ilchulbong early in the morning, walked along the coast, and ate way too many tangerines. But on the third day, out of nowhere, it started pouring rain. We had planned to go to the beach, so Junho and I were really upset, and we kind of complained the whole time. Then my mom, who always has a plan B, found a little black pork restaurant near our hotel. We ended up sitting there for about three hours, grilling meat, listening to the rain, and talking about all kinds of stuff we never talk about at home. Looking back, that rainy night was the best part of the whole trip. It was one of those trips I'll never forget. So yeah, that's my most memorable trip in Korea.

questions.en: How has the way you travel in Korea changed over the years? Compare the trips you took when you were younger with the trips you take now.
questions.ko: 국내 여행하는 방식이 몇 년 사이에 어떻게 바뀌었나요? 어렸을 때의 여행과 지금의 여행을 비교해 주세요.
tips: 답변 흐름: 시작 문장 → 과거(고등학생 때, 가족, 부모님이 계획) → 현재(대학생, 친구들, 앱으로 직접 계획) → 어느 쪽이 좋은지와 이유 → 마무리
'Back in high school, ~ / These days, ~' 처럼 과거·현재 시작 표현을 정해 두세요.
used to + 동사원형으로 과거 습관을 말하면 비교가 분명해집니다.

answers.IM3: Okay, let me tell you how my trips have changed. When I was younger, I used to travel with my family. My parents planned everything, and we went by car. These days, I usually travel with my friends. We plan everything by ourselves on our phones, and we take the KTX. Now we spend more time at cafés and restaurants. Both are fun, but I like traveling with my friends more because it's more free. Yeah, that's how my trips have changed.
answers.IH: Sure, I'd love to talk about that. My trips have changed a lot. Back in high school, I used to travel only with my family. My parents planned everything, and we usually drove somewhere close, like the beach in Gangneung. I just sat in the back seat and listened to music. These days, I'm a college student, so I usually travel with my friends, like Minji. We plan everything by ourselves. We book KTX tickets and places to stay on apps, and we find restaurants by reading reviews online. Also, our trips are more about food and cafés now, not just sightseeing. Of course, traveling with my family was more comfortable because I didn't have to worry about anything. But traveling with friends feels more free and exciting. So yeah, that's pretty much how my trips have changed.
answers.AL: Oh, how my trips have changed? Let me think. Honestly, they've changed a lot over the past few years. Back in high school, I used to travel only with my family, and my parents took care of literally everything. They picked the place, booked the hotel, and drove us there, so all I had to do was sit in the back seat with my earphones in and sleep. Most of our trips were pretty simple, like going to the beach or visiting relatives. These days, it's a totally different story. Now that I'm in college, I mostly travel with my friends, especially Minji, and we plan everything ourselves on our phones. We compare KTX times, book cheap guesthouses on apps, and spend hours reading reviews to find the best local food. Our trips are also much more about the experience now, like trying famous dwaeji-gukbap in Busan or finding a café with an ocean view, rather than just seeing famous spots. To be honest, I miss how easy it was when my parents handled everything. But I love the freedom I have now, and I feel like I've grown up a little by planning trips on my own. Yeah, that's how the way I travel has changed.

pronunciation.tip: '비-치'처럼 '이' 소리를 길게 늘이세요. 짧게 말하면 전혀 다른 단어로 들릴 수 있어요.
첫 음절 '메'에 강세. '메머러블'처럼 뒤는 약하게 흘려요.
'컴프터블' 세 음절처럼 말해요. 'com-for-ta-ble'로 또박또박 끊지 마세요.
